notes:
High-priority enterprise telecom account (EMEA). The whole evaluation is anchored on EU data residency + predictable Dedicated throughput.

What they care about (verbatim-ish):
- "Residency is not a slide—it's a requirement." They want EU-only processing and storage, plus clarity on human access (support/engineering) and auditability.
- Dedicated capacity: wants to eliminate noisy-neighbor risk and have stable tail latency. They asked for concrete sizing assumptions and how Redwood handles bursts.
- Procurement/legal: will push standard MSA/DPA pack; they want subprocessor change notifications and explicit residency language.

Key technical asks:
- Dedicated: clear throughput guarantees, recommended autoscaling/burst approach (even if narrative), and how quotas/rate limits will be set for multiple teams.
- Routing/fallback: allowed only within EU unless explicit customer opt-in. They asked for a way to "prove" routing policy in configuration / audit trail.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown and retention controls for logs/metrics/traces; show audit logs in a safe way.

Current status: Procurement stage with security gating. Technical interest is strong, but closing depends on written residency and acceptable DPA/SLA language. They will not start a pilot until SSO/SAML and audit logging are demonstrated in their format, and residency boundaries are documented.

Internal follow-ups:
- Provide EU-only architecture + support-access boundary statement (coordinate with Security/Compliance: Naomi Feldman, Marcus Lin).
- Confirm what we can commit to regarding EU-only human access and break-glass procedures.
- Prepare Dedicated capacity proposal with clear assumptions (req/min, token distribution, peak hours) and a conservative recommended config.
- Keep demo artifacts in "backup mode" ready; Summit is skeptical of live console data unless it looks deterministic and residency-safe.
